Review issue 103

<pasted_content id="f962">
Closes #103

What: Lets the store owner choose what a product duplicate copies. The Duplicate Product drawer now has four checkboxes, for images, variants, prices and inventory settings, and the duplicate endpoint takes a matching `include` object. Basic product information and options are always copied, and stock quantities still never are.

Why: Duplication copied a fixed set of attributes, so making a similar product meant copying everything and then deleting what you didn't want. My claim comment and the answers to the issue's two open questions are on #103.

How: The groups are resolved in one pure function, `resolveDuplicateProductInclude`, which fills in anything the request left out and applies the one dependency: prices and inventory settings live on the variants, so neither is copied when variants aren't. `buildDuplicateProductInput` then branches on the resolved groups, and the per-variant mapping moved into its own `buildVariant` helper. Both are plain functions called from `transform`, so the whole behavior is unit testable without a database.

Three ACs already held before this branch, so they are covered by tests rather than new code: stock quantities were never copied, the copy was always a draft with new IDs, and the drawer already redirected on success. AC9 had no automated test, so I added one for the redirect and one for the failure path.

Two things worth knowing about the backend. Options are copied unconditionally, because `createProductsWorkflow` throws `Product options are not provided` for a product with none, so unchecking variants gives a product with its options and no variants. And unchecking inventory settings omits `manage_inventory` and `allow_backorder` rather than setting them, so the copy falls back to the product module's defaults. That means a variant whose original has `manage_inventory: false` comes back managed. That is the reading of "not copied" I took from the issue, it is asserted in an integration test rather than left implicit, and it is the one decision here I would most like a second opinion on.

Asking for prices without variants is ignored rather than rejected. With no variants there is nothing to attach a price to, so there is only one sensible result, and the drawer disables those checkboxes anyway. The alternative, a 400, would refuse a request whose intent is clear.

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing is manual-only. The gap worth naming is the same one as on #97: I have not clicked these checkboxes in a running dashboard. AC1, AC2, AC3, AC8 and AC9 are covered at the component level, through the rendered checkboxes, the payload the drawer sends and the navigate and toast calls it makes, not end to end in a browser.

AI-written tests: all three test files on this branch were drafted with Claude Code, and so was the implementation. No expected value was copied from the output of code this PR adds. The defaults and the group names come from AC2 and AC3, the dependency expectations from AC8, and the inventory fallback values from the model defaults in `product-variant.ts`, which I read rather than ran.

I checked the two branches that carry the most behavior by breaking them and watching the tests fail, not just by reading the passes. Removing the `variants &&` guard from `resolveDuplicateProductInclude` failed exactly one test, `forces prices and inventory settings off when variants are off`. Setting `manage_inventory` and `allow_backorder` unconditionally instead of spreading them failed three, including two of the combination tests. Dropping `replace: true` from the redirect and navigating on error failed the two new AC9 tests. All three were reverted afterwards.

One correction during the work: the first version of the dashboard spec declared the navigate and toast spies as plain `const`s, and every test in the file failed to collect, because `vi.mock` factories are hoisted above them. They are declared through `vi.hoisted` now, which is what the file already did for the SDK's bare globals.


The duplicate product spec itself goes from 7 tests to 18, and the dashboard form spec from 4 to 13.

Already failing before this branch, unchanged by it: the 12 HTTP type mismatches are the 10 from #98 plus the 2 the bundles work added, and none of them is a product duplication type. `AdminDuplicateProduct` passes.

The dashboard typecheck does not pass outright, so to be precise about it: `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/admin/dashboard/tsconfig.json` exits 2 with 6 errors, all of them `TS1205` "Re-exporting a type when 'isolatedModules' is enabled requires using 'export type'", 4 in `packages/core/types/src/modules-sdk/index.ts` and 2 in `packages/core/types/src/dal/index.ts`. Both files are byte-identical to develop and neither is touched by this branch, so all 6 predate it. No error is in any file this PR changes, which is the part I can claim credit for rather than the suite being green. `@medusajs/icons` fails 464 of 464 and `@medusajs/ui` 3 of 40, both from the React 19 and React 18 mismatch in #98, which is why the dashboard numbers above are the dashboard package only. CI doesn't run on PRs here, so these runs stand in for it.

One flake worth recording rather than hiding. Running `__tests__/product/admin/` in parallel, `product-imports.spec.ts` failed once with `ENOENT ... T/uploads/test.csv`. It passes 6 of 6 on its own and all 8 suites pass with `--runInBand`, so it is suites sharing one temp upload directory across workers, not this branch: nothing here touches imports or file uploads. That is why the integration command above uses `--runInBand`.

This branch adds no new i18n failures, and because that is the opposite of what my own #97 had to report, here is the measurement rather than the claim. I ran `validate-translation.js` over all 33 locale files twice, once with this branch's `$schema.json` and once with develop's, and counted every error line. Develop's schema gives 5216 across all locales; this branch gives 5215. Exactly one locale's count changes, `en.json`, from 1 to 0, because develop's schema does not know the `include` keys and flags them as `Unexpected key`; the schema commit is what fixes that. All 32 non-English locales come out byte-identical, and no error line in any of them mentions `include`.

The reason this differs from #97, since a reviewer looking at both tonight will reasonably expect them to match: `promotions.export` was a new required key under `promotions`, and `promotions` is present in every locale, so the requirement fired in all 32. `products.duplicate` is present only in `en.json`, because #82 added it there and nowhere else, exactly as my own #63 did for `promotions.duplicate`. Every non-English locale therefore already reports `Missing required key: "duplicate" at /products`, and a missing parent is reported without descending into it, so a new required key inside `duplicate` cannot fire. The two PRs disclose the same thing; the schemas just sit at different depths.

## Tech Debt

Introduced: unchecking inventory settings omits the two fields instead of setting them, so the copy takes the product module's defaults rather than the original's values, and a variant whose original does not manage inventory comes back managed. The issue says the settings are "not copied" without saying what the copy should then have, and omitting is the reading I took. The integration test asserts it so the behavior is documented rather than discovered. If the intended behavior is to carry `manage_inventory: false` across, that is a one-line change in `buildVariant` and a changed assertion.

Introduced: AC1 asks for a modal and this is the drawer #82 already shipped, extended with the checkboxes. Replacing it with a centered modal would change the duplicate flow for a reason unrelated to this issue, and "redesigning the product forms" is out of scope on #103. Flagging it because it is a literal mismatch with AC1's wording.

Introduced: unchecking images does not drop the `thumbnail`, which is a separate column and falls under the "basic product information is always copied" rule in AC2. A copy can therefore show a thumbnail while its image gallery is empty. The original keeps its images so the URL still resolves. I did not invent a rule the issue does not state, but this is the one place where the literal reading gives an odd result, and it is worth a decision on the issue.

Introduced: asking for prices or inventory settings without variants is silently ignored rather than rejected. The reasoning is above. The cost is that a direct API caller gets no signal that part of the request did nothing.

Introduced: the four group names are spelled out in five places, the zod validator, the HTTP type, the workflow type, the `INCLUDE_FIELDS` list in the drawer and the i18n schema. Adding a fifth group means touching all five. A shared constant would need the zod schema and the TypeScript type generated from one source, which the repo does not do for any other payload.

Encountered: the 32 non-English locales are already red on develop, on `fields.operation`, the `wrongQuantity_one` plural key and a long tail of others, between 46 and 349 error lines each. This branch does not add to any of them, for the structural reason given above: they are all missing the `products.duplicate` parent already, so the `include` block this PR requires inside it never gets evaluated. I am recording it here anyway so this reads consistently against #97, where the same kind of schema change did add one key to each of the 32, because `promotions.export` sat under a parent every locale has. Translating the locales is out of scope for both.

Encountered: `scripts/i18n/generate-schema.js` reorders an unrelated `stepsCompletedLabel_*` block when run, because the committed `$schema.json` is stale against `en.json` on develop. I hand-inserted the `include` block instead of committing the generator's output, to keep this diff to the keys the PR adds. Regenerating the schema properly is its own chore.

Encountered: `packages/core/types/src/http/product/admin/payloads.ts` is not Prettier clean on develop, at the `AdminCreateProduct.options` union. Running Prettier on the file reformats that block, so I reverted that hunk and left it as it is on develop.

Encountered: `integration-tests/http` needs `yarn build` of its own before the HTTP suites run, otherwise `medusa-config.js` fails on `./dist/utils/providers/...`. Not caused by this branch, but it is not in the test command in CLAUDE.md and it cost me a run.

Encountered: the duplicate workflow still reads every field in `DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_FIELDS` even when a group is not being copied, so unchecking images or variants does not make the query smaller. It keeps the query stable and one code path, and the filtering is a pure function over what was loaded. Narrowing the query by selection would be a performance change on its own.

```text
+/**
+ * The attribute groups a duplicate can copy. Basic product information and
+ * options are always copied and are not listed here. Any group left out
+ * defaults to being copied, so a request that selects nothing duplicates the

+export type DuplicateProductInclude = {

+  images?: boolean
+  /**

+  variants?: boolean

+  inventory_settings?: boolean

+/**

+ * them: prices and inventory settings are stored on variants, so neither can
+ * be copied when variants are not.
+ *
+ * Everything defaults to copied, which is what duplication did before the
+ * groups existed, so an unchanged request behaves as it always has.
+ */
+export const resolveDuplicateProductInclude = (
+  include?: DuplicateProductInclude
+): Required<DuplicateProductInclude> => {
+  const variants = include?.variants ?? true
+
+  return {
+    images: include?.images ?? true,
+    variants,
+    prices: variants && (include?.prices ?? true),
+    inventory_settings: variants && (include?.inventory_settings ?? true),
+  }
+}
```

## Code Review: #103, choosing what a product duplicate copies

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | 9 | All four groups work across the validator, workflow, SDK, types and drawer. `resolveDuplicateProductInclude` handles the variants dependency cleanly, and leaving `include` out still copies everything, so older callers keep working. AC1 asked for a modal and this extends the existing drawer, which the PR says openly. The open behavior question is below. |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | 9 | Strong. There are unit, component and integration tests, and the expected values come from the ACs and model defaults, not from running the new code. The mutation checks (breaking the `variants &&` guard, the spread and `replace: true`) are good evidence. I re-ran the core-flows spec (24/24 pass) and the dashboard form spec (13/13 pass). |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | Pulling `buildVariant` out keeps the diff readable, and options always being copied is well explained. Small nit: `t(labelKey as any)` in [duplicate-product-form.tsx](packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/product-duplicate/components/duplicate-product-form/duplicate-product-form.tsx) could be avoided by typing `labelKey` as a union of the four literal keys. The group names are spelled out in five places, which the PR already lists as debt. |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | 7 | The comments and TSDoc are clear and explain the reasons. The description has one wrong claim and one stale string (see below). It is also very long. The i18n locale-count section could shrink to two lines. |
| AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 10 | It says plainly that Claude Code drafted the work, explains where each expected value came from, gives the mutation results, and admits the `vi.hoisted` correction. This is how it should be done. |
| Overall: would you merge this as-is? | 8 | Yes, after the two small fixes below. Nothing blocks it. |

**Small fixes before merge:**
1. **Wrong test count in the PR description.** It says "The duplicate product spec itself goes from 7 tests to 18." The file `packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/__tests__/duplicate-product.spec.ts` doesn't exist on develop, and on this branch it has 24 tests. Suggest: "adds a new unit spec with 24 tests". The dashboard figure (4 to 13) is correct.
2. **Stale drawer copy.** In `en.json`, `products.duplicate.description` still says "Create a draft copy of this product with its options, variants, prices and images." That is no longer always true. Suggest something like "Create a draft copy of this product. Choose what to copy below."

**On the decision you asked for a second opinion on (inventory settings):** I think omitting the fields is the defensible reading of "not copied", and it's documented and tested. One side effect is worth adding to Tech Debt: since `manage_inventory` defaults to `true`, unchecking inventory settings makes the copy create inventory items for variants whose original had none. A store owner might not expect that. It's worth a one-line confirmation on the issue, not a code change.

---

I skipped the HTTP integration suite, the build and the i18n validation. Those results come from the PR description, not from my own runs. I also didn't click through the drawer in a running dashboard, which the PR names as its own gap too.
